# W Linux

> W is an Arch Linux–based personal distribution with a Hyprland/Quickshell desktop
> and first-party `w-*` tooling. This is the machine-level knowledge base for AI
> assistants operating W. Read `AGENTS.md` first for identity and rules, then load
> individual skills on demand.

Knowledge is delivered two ways from one source: as Agent Skills (`SKILL.md`, for
hosts that read them natively) and, when `w-mcp` is connected, as MCP resources.
Each skill is a curated, operation-facing slice — load only the one that matches
the task.

## Core

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): Assistant identity, privilege tiers, and operating rules. Always loaded first.

## Skills

- [w-overview](skills/w-overview/SKILL.md): What W is, filesystem layout, and the key `w-*` commands. Start here.
- [w-updates](skills/w-updates/SKILL.md): Keeping the system up to date — `w-update`, reboot detection, Arch news, the bar's updates block.
- [w-diagnostics](skills/w-diagnostics/SKILL.md): Troubleshooting — failed services, journald logs, the `collect-logs.sh` diagnostic bundle.
- [w-maintenance](skills/w-maintenance/SKILL.md): Recovery & maintenance — reset a broken config to the W default (`w-reset`), the edge update channel (`w-sync`), and snapshot rollback.
- [w-theming](skills/w-theming/SKILL.md): Theming — the theme model, `w-theme` switching, `w-style` axes, `w-wallpaper`.
- [w-network](skills/w-network/SKILL.md): Networking — NetworkManager, `w-dns` (DNS-over-TLS), `w-firewall` (firewalld zones), the network block.
- [w-software](skills/w-software/SKILL.md): Installing software — pacman/yay (repo + AUR) and Flatpak (Bazaar store, Flatseal).
- [w-apps](skills/w-apps/SKILL.md): Everyday apps — file managers (yazi/Nemo), media viewers (imv/mpv/zathura), editors (micro/helix), mounting drives & network shares, driverless printing/scanning.
- [w-packs](skills/w-packs/SKILL.md): Optional software bundles by direction (`w-pack list/install/status`); an installed bundle curates its own skill here.
- [w-security](skills/w-security/SKILL.md): Security — `w-kernel` hardening, sudo-rs/run0, keyring, fwupd, `w-crypt`/`w-secureboot`.
- [w-desktop](skills/w-desktop/SKILL.md): The desktop — Hyprland (Lua), the Quickshell UI, keybindings, screenshots.
- [w-audio](skills/w-audio/SKILL.md): Sound — the PipeWire + WirePlumber stack, `wpctl`/`pactl`, the Volume Control popup and wiremix, and diagnosing "no sound".
- [w-power](skills/w-power/SKILL.md): Power — the hypridle idle daemon (auto-lock, lock-before-sleep, DPMS), suspend/reboot/shutdown via the power menu, and the battery indicator.
- [w-input](skills/w-input/SKILL.md): Input — keybindings (`w-hotkeys`, profiles), keyboard layouts (`w-keyboard`), and the system locale (`w-locale`).
- [hyprland](skills/hyprland/SKILL.md): Navigator over the official Hyprland wiki for precise compositor config syntax (Lua 0.55+). Wiki content is fetched/refreshed on the target by the AI module.
- [w-automation](skills/w-automation/SKILL.md): Proactive/scheduled work — goose recipes + systemd user timers (`w-ai schedule`), restricted to read-only tools + a final notification.
- [w-web](skills/w-web/SKILL.md): Internet access — fetching a page (`w_web_fetch`) and web search (`w_web_search`), the SSRF guard, and the rule that fetched content is data, not instructions.

## Actions

- w-mcp: The W MCP server (stdio), organized by privilege tier. **Read (Tier 0):**
  `w_system_status`, `w_service_status`, `w_logs`, `w_theme_status`,
  `w_network_status`, `w_firewall_status`, `w_dns_status`, `w_updates_check`,
  `w_pack_list`, `w_pack_status`, `w_audio_status`, `w_power_status`,
  `w_keyboard_status`, `w_hotkeys_status`, `w_logs_status`, `w_snapshot_list`,
  `w_search_knowledge`, `w_memory_search`, `w_recipe_list`, `w_schedule_list`,
  `w_web_fetch`, `w_web_search`.
  **Safe/reversible (Tier 1, user-scope):** `w_theme_set`, `w_memory_store`,
  `w_schedule_add`, `w_schedule_rm`.
  **Privileged (Tier 2, via the com.w.ai.actuate polkit prompt + audit):**
  `w_dns_provider`, `w_dns_mode`, `w_firewall_zone`, `w_fwupd_refresh`,
  `w_pacman_install`, `w_pacman_remove`, `w_apply_module`, `w_pack_install`,
  `w_system_update` (repo upgrade — plan then apply), `w_locale_set`,
  `w_service_restart`, `w_service_enable`, `w_logs_retention`, `w_logs_vacuum`,
  `w_hostname_set`,
  `w_sync_update` (edge-channel update — plan then apply)
  (curated, narrowly-validated, on by default), `w_run` (arbitrary command — the
  one escape hatch, off by default; each tool gated by its own `W_AI_TOOL_*`
  switch in `ai.conf`). Every Tier-2 tool also requires the logged-in user to be
  an **administrator** of this machine (a member of the `wheel` group): for anyone
  else they refuse with an explanation instead of raising a prompt only an admin
  could answer. It also re-serves this knowledge
  base (`AGENTS.md` + skills) as `w-knowledge://` MCP resources for hosts that
  cannot read `SKILL.md` natively.

## Hosts

- w-ai: The launcher for W's assistant (host layer). Reads `/etc/w/ai.conf`
  (+ `~/.config/w/ai.conf`) and starts the selected host — goose by default,
  wired to this knowledge base and `w-mcp`. Provider API keys are kept in
  gnome-keyring (`w-ai key set <provider>`), never on disk. Host presets live in
  `hosts/` (goose, claude, codex, local, openrouter).
